html:
Under British rule from 1810, Mauritius was turned almost entirely over to sugar cane, and by the mid 19th century it was one of the main sugar producers of the British Empire.

The French-descended planters relied on enslaved Africans and Malagasy until slavery was ended in 1835, with compensation paid to the owners. They then brought hundreds of thousands of indentured labourers from India, whose descendants now make up most of the population.

Sugar dominated the economy, the landscape and politics until the 1970s. Guaranteed prices in Britain and later Europe paid for the start of the economic boom. Cane still covers much of the farmland, and the old estates are now turning to tourism and housing. It links Mauritius to the history of sugar worldwide.
sum: Under British rule from 1810, Mauritius was turned almost entirely over to sugar cane, and by the mid 19th century it was one of the main sugar producers of the British Empire.
